We now double-check if the sample size is sufficient, assuming we find the same proportion of women in the additional sample of 41 items (overall $k' = 0.62 \cdot 91 = 56.4$, rounded to 57). This gives us

\begin{equation*}
p_l = \frac{57}{57 + (91 - 57 + 1) \cdot 1.511} = 0.519
\end{equation*}
and the upper bound as
\begin{equation*}
p_u = \frac{57 + 1}{57 + 1 + (91 - 57)/1.550} = 0.726
\end{equation*}

The interval estimate is reduced to [51.9\%, 72.6\%].
